summary: Explains building a collection tarball: bump the version in galaxy.yml (versions are immutable and duplicates fail with conflict.collection_exists), run ansible-galaxy collection build, and note default exclusions and Galaxy's 20 MB size limit.
questions: Why do I get conflict.collection_exists when publishing?
How do I build the tarball for my collection?
What's the maximum collection size Galaxy accepts?
Can I distribute a collection without uploading it to Galaxy?

answer_card.title: Build a collection tarball
answer_card.answer_md:
1. Review `galaxy.yml` and **bump the version**. Published versions can't change; re-uploading the same version fails with `Code: conflict.collection_exists`. Use semantic versioning.
2. From the collection root: `ansible-galaxy collection build` produces e.g. `my_namespace-my_collection-1.0.0.tar.gz`.

Some files are excluded by default. Galaxy's max tarball size is **20 MB**. You can also copy the tarball to targets and install it directly.
